name: stonewall-tactical-a
prompt: Create a production game-art atlas for FRONTLINES, a stylized illustrated military science-fiction strategy card game. ONE square 2048x2048 image, divided into EXACTLY FOUR equal square full-bleed paintings in a 2-by-2 grid, no gutters, no margins, no frames, no text, no numbers, no symbols or typography. The four paintings never overlap across the exact vertical and horizontal midlines. Each is polished painted graphic-novel military concept art: convincing anatomy, coherent equipment, worn steel surfaces, cinematic lighting, strong readable silhouette and clear tactical role. Style is detailed illustrated realism, not a photograph, not simple flat vector art, not anime. These are ordinary tactical cards, not portraits of commanding officers. STONEWALL faction throughout: disciplined defenders, angular reinforced gray armor, cool cyan visor/equipment accents, concrete fortifications, rain and restrained warm light in a battered sci-fi city. Each main subject's face/helmet AND distinctive equipment must be immediately readable in a small crop; keep identifying features safely within the central 70 percent of each tile. Vary camera angles and composition intentionally. Tile TOP LEFT: Trench Engineer, a kneeling armored military engineer installing and welding a waist-high armored barricade, glowing hand tool, defensive trench, protectively hunched silhouette. Tile TOP RIGHT: Shield Section, two disciplined armored defenders advancing behind overlapping massive rectangular riot shields while impacts spark off the shields, diagonal shield wall, determined tactical formation. Tile BOTTOM LEFT: Bastion Gunner, a heavily armored gunner braced behind a large mounted heavy machine gun on a fortified firing line, weapon pointing diagonally toward camera, cool cyan optics. Tile BOTTOM RIGHT: Field Mechanic, a practical armored repair specialist using a bright diagnostic tool to repair a damaged deployed armored turret, open panel and careful hands, deliberate engineering rather than combat shooting. Do not repeat the same generic soldier pose. No logos, no captions, no abstract icon artwork, no UI, no excessive bloom.
